name: Luminous Sect
reason: Source sect name 'Iridescent Clouds Sect' was simplified to 'Luminous Sect', keeping the light imagery while fitting the adaptation's cleaner Western fantasy register.
description: A Grade Two sect under Cloud Hall, led by Lady Sigmund (source: Granny Long of the Iridescent Clouds Sect). Its disciples are mostly women; top disciple Lois is betrothed to Frank. Members of the sect take part in the Death Road / Trialtakers trial arc around Eps 359-385.

name: Elder Howard
reason: The character's Chinese surname-plus-title 'Elder Wei' was fully localized; 'Howard' was chosen as a warm, dignified US-origin name befitting a kindly senior elder, keeping the 'Elder' title.
description: A friendly elder at the Rising Dragon Platform who recruits and mentors Zane after watching him climb the obelisks (Eps 438-450). Warm and patient, he guides Zane through the first trials of the new area and favors him over Elder Julian's protege. Matches source Elder Wei (chs 425-437), who guides Luo Zheng through the obelisk trial.

name: High-tier
issues: Recurring grammar artifact 'an High-tier' (Eps 58, 65) suggests a find-and-replace from a vowel-initial source term ('Innate'). Also overlaps with the later 'Nature Level'/'Nature Spirit' rendering of the same source Xiantian/Innate tier - possible early-episode term drift.
reason: The source cultivation tier 'Xiantian/Innate Realm' was rendered 'High-tier' in early episodes to avoid untranslated cultivation jargon; 'High-tier candidate' corresponds to the source's 'Half-step to Innate Realm'.
description: An early-arc cultivation tier label (Eps 44-82) ranking above Zane's Marrow Refining Level. 'High-tier candidates' are warriors a half-step from the full tier; missions and transport vessels use it as a minimum strength requirement. Corresponds to the source's Xiantian (Innate) Realm.

name: Heavenly Tribulation
reason: The source's English term 'Heavenly Tribulation' was kept unchanged, as it already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: A punishment sent down by the heavens on warriors who grow too strong, typically striking at breakthroughs. Zane faces and dodges successive Heavenly Tribulations (up to a Tenth, Eps 1108-1109), and it is also the name of the third layer of a thunder-principle set (Annihilation, Purification, Heavenly Tribulation, Ep 879). One is even summoned against Lance in Ep 1215.

name: Lesser Celestial Tribulation
reason: The source's 'minor Heaven's Tribulation' (faced in the Life and Death Realm) was renamed 'Lesser Celestial Tribulation' for a more elevated Western fantasy tone and to distinguish it from the full Heavenly Tribulation.
description: The smaller tribulation a warrior must survive to advance within the Life-and-Death Realm, described as a baptism by fire. Variants include the rare Nightmare Tribulation. Zane faces his first on The Feather Emperor's Island and later expects another when breaking through to the realm's second level (Eps 875-978).

name: Willow Island
reason: The source island 'Changsu Island' was localized as 'Willow Island', replacing the Chinese place name with a simple nature-based Western name.
description: A continent-sized island in the Upper Realm, the site of the Passing the Torch event (source: Torch Flame Inheritance on Changsu Island, chs 1044-1111). Warriors of the Thirteen Palaces swarm it during the event, and a great rock formation at its edge draws meditating Soul Sea Realm warriors seeking insight (Eps 1067-1129).

name: Yosef
reason: The source character is only ever titled (the Demon Race's Saint Lord, master of the Demon Clan's Holy Land); the adaptation gave him the personal name 'Yosef' and localized his race as 'ogres'.
description: The Ogre Saint Lord, ruler of the ogres' sacred place and a quasi-Sector-Lord-level power (source: the Demon Race's Saint Lord). He covets the Wheel of Reincarnation as it rises and delivers an ultimatum over it, skirting his agreement by not actually killing anyone (Eps 1137-1168).

name: Eight Smoky Melodies
reason: The source technique 'Eight Winding Smoke' was renamed 'Eight Smoky Melodies', keeping the number and smoke imagery while adding a more lyrical ring.
description: Zane's signature defensive evasion technique in the late arcs (Eps 1205-1317): white mist curls off him and automatically carries him out of the path of attacks, triggering even against blows he cannot consciously react to. It has saved his life repeatedly, including against Sloane's decapitating strike, though overwhelming attacks can still slip through.

name: Upper Realm
reason: The source's English term 'Upper Realm' (also rendered 'Upper World' by the translator) was kept as-is.
description: The higher world above Zane's native lower realm, home to vastly stronger clans and rarer treasures; ascending to it is a major goal tied to the Dragon Soar Arena pathway (Ep 455). Even divine weapons are rare there, and powers like the Demon Night measure their elites by its standards (Eps 455-996).

name: Mad Scorpion
reason: Source creature 'Vicious Scorpion' was renamed 'Mad Scorpion' for the Western fantasy setting, keeping the beast's menacing register.
description: A mountain-sized colossal scorpion beast encountered at the edge of a chasm (Eps 663-680). It battles the Celestial Root in a clash that tears up over a thousand feet of ground, and Zane's party, including Malcolm and Esther, ends up inside its body. Matches the source's Vicious Scorpion (chs ~644-653).

name: Heavenly Stellar Palace
reason: The source location 'Tianchen Palace' (tianchen = 'heavenly star') was translated literally as 'Heavenly Stellar Palace'.
description: Zane's rune-warded palace residence in Oracle City (source: Tianchen Palace in Tianqi City, chs ~744-933). He summons Lavender there, receives the leaders of the World Merchants' Guild outside it, and it withstands probing assassins; hundreds of defensive runes blaze to life when he lands (Eps 766-955).

name: Hanson Lee
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Li Hetai' was fully localized; the surname Li became the common Western equivalent 'Lee', and 'Hanson' was chosen as an unassuming given name fitting a humble beggar.
description: A beggar who answers Zane's notice seeking Raw Vitality, revealing he buried seven heartstones outside Oracle City (Eps 767-774; source: Li Hetai, chs ~745-750). Zane promises him a place in Cloud Hall and a thousand supreme Aether crystals from the Guild, and the talk of Soul Sea Realm warriors leaves his head spinning.

name: Edwin
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Edwin' was chosen as a solid, slightly aristocratic name for the Martial House's champion fighter.
description: The top young fighter of the Crystal Martial House (source: Zhan Yun, number one False Tribulation Realm warrior of the Black/Profound Jade Martial House, chs 764-782). He steamrolls opponents in the Martial House arena assessment, wields a limb-slicing Spatial Blade, and is roped in by the Crown Prince to fight on his behalf against Randy's side (Eps 790-805).

name: Slow Arrow Field
reason: The source zone (translated variously as 'Arrow Slow Zone' / 'Arrow Retardation Area', ch 821) was smoothed into the cleaner English name 'Slow Arrow Field'.
description: A hazardous jungle region in a trial area (Eps 838-846) filled with punishing phantom arrows that vanish once travelers clear the zone. Randy's group, following Fredrick's lead, takes a beating crossing it before reaching the pitch-black grassland of the Spectral Plains beyond.

name: Wade
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Ha Peng' was fully localized; 'Wade' was chosen as a short, easygoing US-origin name matching his relaxed, jokey demeanor.
description: A member of Boss Mo's crew (source: Ha Peng, chs ~891-931) who pilots The Compass Wheel (source: Eight Trigrams Wheel), ferrying the group to and from Oracle City. He binds the Evil Dragon with his fishing-rod restraints until it breaks free, and he banters cheerfully despite his female companion's death threats (Eps 914-954).

name: Tower of Crystal
reason: The source treasure 'Linglong Pagoda' (also translated 'Exquisite Pagoda') was renamed 'Tower of Crystal', trading the Chinese name for a concrete Western image of its preciousness.
description: A long-lost, priceless pagoda treasure hunted by the Demi-Immortal group (Eps 920-928; source: the Linglong/Exquisite Pagoda, chs ~897-946). Dorothea Garrison discovers its whereabouts, and a Mark later confirms Zane had been inside it, making him the group's target despite the Evil Dragon's interference.

name: Lacey
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Lan Bing' was fully localized; 'Lacey' was chosen as a light, feminine US-origin name for the barrier-wielding warrior.
description: A female warrior (source: Lan Bing, chs ~920-926) who holds a defensive barrier for her group during the clash with the Demon Race forces (Eps 943-949). She repeatedly bites the tip of her tongue to burn essence blood for bursts of power, matching the source's Water Ripple Domain fighter who does exactly this against Mo Xiao's experts.

name: Legendary Weapon
issues: Term appears only in early episodes (21-143) and is not part of the show's later canonical weapon-tier ladder (Mysterious/Spirit/Mythic/Sacred/Divine); likely early-batch grade naming that was superseded.
reason: The source grade 'Upper Grade Xuan (Profound) Weapon' was rendered 'Legendary Weapon' in early episodes to convey top-grade rarity without cultivation jargon.
description: An early-arc label for the rarest grade of weapon: even House Lowell, rulers of Castermere County, own only one, the Greenwind Blade of Zane's father (Ep 21). Evil Jace's Hellfire Blade is another example (Ep 61), mirroring the source where the Zi Qing Sword and Karmic Fire Sword are both high-grade profound weapons.

name: Nature Spirit
issues: Overlaps with 'High-tier' (Eps 44-82): both early-episode terms appear to render the source Xiantian/Innate tier, suggesting term drift before 'Nature Level' settled as canon.
reason: Source cultivators of the Xiantian (Innate) stage were localized as 'Nature Spirits', matching the show's 'Nature Level' naming for that tier.
description: A term for warriors who have reached the Nature Level (source: Xiantian stage), whose lifespan extends to a minimum of one hundred and fifty years (Ep 76). A Nature Spirit vastly outclasses ordinary cultivators, making a loss to a mere refiner shocking (Ep 85).

name: Emerald Sword
issues: Possible merged entity: the name is used for weapons of different owners - Seymour's sword (Ep 154), Jill's small blade (Ep 272, per master sheet), and another warrior's wind-forged blade (Ep 1035) - likely distinct source weapons sharing one localized name.
reason: An adaptation-side weapon name; no single source counterpart is evidenced, and the name appears to have been reused for several green-themed blades.
description: A green-glowing sword name appearing across widely separated arcs: Seymour's blade flares with green light in Ep 154, Jill wins nearly every match by pressing hers to opponents' necks around Ep 272, and in Ep 1035 a warrior reforges his Emerald Sword's blade from spinning wind currents.

name: Immortal Profound Flame
reason: A flame-barrier term from the Passing the Torch arc; the exact source term is not evidenced in the provided candidates, so the mapping is left open.
description: An ancient flame barring Zane's path during the Passing the Torch trials (Eps 1083-1086). Even at less than a hundred-thousandth of its original power it is considered impassable by watching warriors, and Lavender notes it cannot be truly extinguished.

name: Immortal
reason: A title-style name for an ancient dead power from the source's tomb arcs; no pinyin name is evidenced, so the source identity is left unmatched.
description: An ancient, long-dead being whose soul fragments retain terrifying power and cunning: an enemy fuses with one remnant in Eps 163-164, and the Celestial Tomb is an Immortal's resting place holding invaluable treasures (Ep 483; 'The Immortal's Coffin', Ep 551).

name: Seventeenth Court
reason: The source location 'Seventeenth Courtyard' (also translated 'Seventeenth Academy') was tightened to 'The Seventeenth Court' for the adaptation.
description: A courtyard compound within the sect where Zane works at his furnace (Eps 215-220; source: Seventeenth Courtyard, chs 200-204). A razor-sharp beam of energy from the furnace famously slices clean through one of its walls.

name: Head of Cloud Hall
reason: The leadership title of the source organization Cloud Hall, rendered plainly as 'Head of Cloud Hall'; the exact source title is not evidenced among the candidates.
description: The leadership office of Cloud Hall, the higher organization above the Skyreach Sect. A male Head holds the record of reaching a silver treasure box in the trial road (Eps 374-378); the title later passes - a female holder loses her authority in Ep 458, and Tia becomes the newly appointed head upon ascending to the Life-and-Death Realm (Ep 723).

name: Head
issues: Some captures are noise ('Head south', Ep 708 - a verb, not the title).

name: Soul Power
reason: The source's English term 'Soul Power' was kept unchanged.
description: The energy of a cultivator's soul, used for healing injuries, sensing, and soul-based techniques (Eps 271-1061). It can be depleted - even the Cobalt Dragon's ran dry (Ep 427) - and restored, as when Zane consumes the Owl Beast's evil spirit (Ep 517); cultivating it is a formal training phase at the Rising Dragon Platform (Ep 441).

name: Sacred
reason: Generic adjective fragment, not a standalone entity: its captures belong to already-canonical terms such as the Sacred Arms weapon tier ('Sacred weapon/blades'), the Sacred Lunge technique (Ep 80), and 'Sacred martial artists' as a rank descriptor.

name: Lady Sigmund
reason: The source character 'Granny Long', Sect Master of the Iridescent Clouds Sect, was localized as 'Lady Sigmund'; the honorific 'Lady' replaces 'Granny' and 'Sigmund' gives her sect's leadership a stately Western surname.
description: The sharp-tongued leader of the Luminous Sect, a Grade Two sect under Cloud Hall (Eps 360-402). She carries a cane, is fiercely protective of her disciples Lois and Frank, clashes with Sir Kenneth, and nurses a personal grudge against Zane, belittling him at every appearance. Mirrors the source's Granny Long, who frets over her female disciples in the fire-sea trial.

name: Metal Law
reason: The source's English term 'Metal Law' (also rendered 'Law of Metal') was kept as-is.
description: One of the elemental Laws warriors can comprehend, manifesting as flares of gold power alongside counterparts like Wind Law (Ep 1037). Practitioners can wield it with overpowering force in duels (Ep 1099), and its ultimate attainment is the Form of the Adamant Soul (Ep 1100).

name: Grade-Three Divine Weapon
reason: The source's lowest divine-artifact grade, 'Secondary Grade Three Divine Artifact', was streamlined to 'Grade-Three Divine Weapon' (also phrased 'Grade-Three Divine-Class') for the adaptation's simpler grading scheme.
description: The lowest grade of Divine-Class weapon in the Upper Realm arcs (Eps 1037-1110). Even Emperors of the divine kingdoms wield Grade-Threes, yet warriors of the Thirteen Palaces consider them beginner gear they outgrew decades ago; settling for one stings the pride of ambitious fighters like Ryder Golding's brother.
